page: Microsoft Azure L96ps_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance based on the 64-bit ARM architecture. Running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance provides 96 dedicated ARMv8 64-bit vCPUs paired with 768.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance is provisioned with 23,038 GB of bundled direct-attached NVMe solid-state storage and does not include dedicated graphics processing units or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The inclusion of over 23 TB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage establishes this server's primary engineering focus on high-throughput, low-latency disk operations. Combined with a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory configuration across 96 dedicated processor threads, the hardware profile eliminates disk I/O bottlenecks without requiring external network-attached block devices. However, because it runs on an ARM64 instruction set, workloads must maintain native binary compatibility or support recompilation for ARM architectures.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the L96ps_v5 balances dense non-volatile storage with high compute core counts on energy-efficient ARM silicon. This architectural approach delivers significant local storage density per compute unit compared to standard general-purpose instances. Workloads best aligned with the L96ps_v5 profile include large-scale NoSQL and relational database engines, distributed transactional datastores, big data analytics engines, and write-intensive data ingestion pipelines that demand high local storage capacity alongside massive memory footprints.
description: Microsoft Azure L96ps_v5 is an ARM-based storage-optimized virtual machine powered by 96 dedicated ARM64 vCPUs and 768.0 GB of memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 23,038 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage to deliver substantial local I/O capacity without relying on external network disks. The configuration excludes GPU hardware accelerators and complimentary public IPv4 addresses, directing its capabilities entirely toward compute, RAM density, and direct-attached storage performance. The combination of dense local solid-state storage and high-core ARM processing offers an efficient architecture for storage-heavy deployments. The L96ps_v5 is designed for I/O-intensive workloads, including large relational databases, distributed NoSQL databases, search indexing, streaming telemetry processing, and big data analytics pipelines requiring immediate access to multi-terabyte datasets.
